title: 半山面包：同一页面的三套动效
Banshan Bakery: three motion treatments for one page
summary: 同一个面包店页面和品牌，分别用最低打扰、实体反馈和跟着任务走的动效处理按压、悬停和成功确认。
The same bakery page and brand, with press, hover and success handled three ways: least disturbance, physical feedback, and motion that follows the task.
brief: 给面包店的单页加克制而有用的动效：按钮按压、今日面包列表项的悬停、预订成功提示的出现，在触屏和“减少动效”设置下也要好用。页面是纯 HTML，品牌沿用 style.css。

Add restrained, useful motion to the bakery's one-page site: the button press, hover on today's bread list items, and the appearance of the order confirmation, working on touch screens and under the reduce-motion setting too. Plain HTML; the brand comes from style.css.

optimizes: 最低打扰：按压只加深颜色并缩小 2%，列表悬停只换整行底色帮助对齐，成功提示在按钮下方原地淡入，不移动任何东西。

Least disturbance: a press only darkens the colour and shrinks by 2%, list hover only changes the whole row's background to help alignment, and the success notice fades in below the button in place without moving anything.
tradeoff: 确认感最弱，提示离视线焦点稍远；悬停只是扫读辅助，没有附带动作，对触屏用户等于没有。
The weakest sense of confirmation, with the notice a little away from the point of focus; hover is only a scanning aid with no action attached, so for touch users it is as if it were not there.
bestFor: 想保持原页面单栏阅读感、维护成本最低、访客以手机为主又不想加交互的店主。
A shop owner who wants to keep the original single-column reading feel, the lowest maintenance, mostly phone visitors and no added interaction.

alt: 单栏页面，按钮和列表行只用颜色变化，成功提示在按钮下方
A single-column page where the button and list rows change only colour, with the success notice below the button

optimizes: 实体反馈：按钮有 2px 底边，按下时下沉并压扁到 98%，提交中有进度线；列表悬停长出左侧标记并把价格变品牌色；成功提示条从底部上浮 16px，6 秒后退场，可关闭。桌面端预订面板固定在右侧。

Physical feedback: buttons have a 2px bottom edge, sink and squash to 98% when pressed, and show a progress line while submitting; list hover grows a marker on the left and turns the price brand-coloured; the success bar floats up 16px from the bottom, leaves after 6 seconds and can be dismissed. On desktop the order panel stays fixed on the right.
tradeoff: 动效最多、JS 最多；提示条在手机上可能被软键盘或拇指遮挡，所以表单下方还要保留一行静态确认；下沉效果依赖阴影，减少动效下只剩颜色变化。

The most motion and the most JavaScript; on phones the bar may be hidden by the soft keyboard or a thumb, so a static confirmation line stays under the form; the sinking effect relies on shadow, and under reduced motion only the colour change remains.
bestFor: 桌面访客较多、希望预订入口始终可见（比如公司团购或门店自用的平板点单），以及想要明显“按下去了”手感的场景。
Mostly desktop visitors who want the order entry always in view (a company's group order, or a tablet the shop uses itself), and anywhere a clear 'pressed' feel matters.

alt: 桌面双栏，右侧固定预订面板，按钮带底边
Two desktop columns with the order panel fixed on the right and buttons with a bottom edge

optimizes: 动效跟着任务走：列表行悬停露出“预订这款”（触屏和键盘下始终可见），点选后带到表单；提交按钮按下缩小 3%，成功后按钮自己变成深色确认并画出对勾，详情从 0 高度展开，被订的那一行闪一次“已为你预订 1 个”。

Motion follows the task: hovering a list row reveals 'order this one' (always visible on touch and keyboard), and choosing it leads to the form; the submit button shrinks 3% when pressed, and on success the button itself turns into a dark confirmation and draws a tick, the details expand from zero height, and the ordered row flashes 'reserved 1 for you' once.
tradeoff: 在原任务上加了“选品项”这一步和对应状态，JS 分支最多；按钮变成确认后需要“再订一份”才能重来；对勾描边和展开在减少动效下会退化为直接出现。

Adds a 'choose an item' step and its states to the original task, with the most JavaScript branches; once the button has become the confirmation, 'order another' is needed to start again; the tick stroke and the expansion degrade to appearing at once under reduced motion.
bestFor: 访客以手机为主、面包款式少但余量紧张（需要先抢指定款）的店，以及希望确认信息出现在手指刚按过的位置的场景。
Shops with mostly phone visitors, few kinds of bread and tight stock (customers need to claim a specific loaf first), and anywhere the confirmation should appear where the finger just pressed.

alt: 菜单在前，每行带“预订这款”按钮，表单里多一行品项
The menu first, each row with an 'order this one' button, and an extra item line in the form

reason: 面包店页面的多数访问来自手机，C 把成功确认放在用户刚按下的按钮上，触屏与桌面体验一致，悬停动效也有实际用途（露出“预订这款”）而不是装饰。这是基于动效规则的假设，没有做过用户测试；B 的提示条在手机键盘弹出时可能被遮挡，A 则是最省心、最不依赖 JS 的底线方案。若不想增加“先选品项”这一功能，可以保留 C 的按钮确认但去掉行内动作。

Most visits to a bakery page come from phones. C puts the success confirmation on the button the user just pressed, so touch and desktop behave the same, and its hover motion has a real use (revealing 'order this one') rather than being decoration. This is an assumption based on the motion rules, not user-tested; B's bar may be covered when the phone keyboard opens, and A is the easiest, least JavaScript-dependent baseline. If the 'choose an item first' feature is unwanted, keep C's button confirmation and drop the inline action.
